paths.logic: An assignment states a lasting equality between its two sides, so y = x - y can be solved like the equation x = 2y and x = x + 5 relates two equal quantities.
paths.twin_logic: An assignment is a one-time action: evaluate the right side with current values, then store the result in the left variable.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: Then b = t means b equals a
paths.logic: Points to LT (three assignments in order, each using current values). Applied unevenly, a student traces the first two steps correctly but uses a's original value in the third, or calls one segment a swap and the other a copy without tracing either. (here mixing in: "a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = a[i]; exchanges the two values")

paths.label: broken
paths.logic: The three assignments int t = a; a = b; b = t; exchange the values of a and b, as a trace of the variable values after each statement shows.

evidence.logic: In everyday life two people swap objects at the same moment, hand to hand, and 'b = a' sounds like 'a and b are now the same thing'. Java statements run one at a time, so the first assignment destroys a value unless it was first saved in a temporary.
